newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open more than two pct higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open more than two pct higher.

text.p: French stocks opened more than two percent higher on Wednesday as European share and debt markets rallied in the wake of remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan than inflation remained modest.
The CAC-40 leading share index opened 2.17 percent, or 63.42 points, higher and advanced by close to 2.5 percent in early morning trading.
The CAC-40 stood 2.84 percent higher at 3,004.05 at 0950 GMT after hitting an all-time high in mid-morning trading of 3,007.84.

Greenspan said after European markets closed on Wednesday he was "reasonably confident" that inflation would be quite modest this year and said there was "basic improvement" in the economy as technology boosted productivity.
"The (French) market should hit new highs fast, this week," said one stock market player.
Luxury goods and drinks group LVMH was among the major early gainers, up 3.91 percent at 1,620 francs after saying on Tuesday it has boosted its stake in Grand Metropolitan to more than 10 percent.
It is turning up the pressure on GrandMet and Guinness to agree LVMH's plans for a three-way tie-up.

The market lift produced further gains in banking stocks, which had already gained significantly on Tuesday after a German bank merger had the spill-over effect of renewing speculation of sector restructuring in France.
Big gainers included BNP, more than five percent up at 0915 GMT and CCF close to six percent higher.

Renault was up 4.43 percent at 172.1 francs. Brokerage Ferri said in a note the share price had broken technical resistance near 158-159 francs and should now test 182-185 francs. Car parts maker Valeo surged too.

Cement and building materials group Lafarge marked further big gains after its U.S. unit reported a rise in second quarter profit on Tuesday and predicted substantial profit margin improvement for the third quarter.

Tobacco group Seita bucked the trend, down 0.86 percent at 183.5. Ferri brokerage said Seita volumes could fall more heavily than a 4.1 percent drop in French tobacco market in the first half of the year.
